cards.name: History
cards.summary: Shows or hides the History panel, the list of the document's recent edit states in order; clicking an earlier state steps the document back to it, and making a new edit from there discards the later states. The panel makes no edits of its own.
use_for: stepping back several edits at once to compare an earlier state of a logo
recovering from a run of bad edits without undoing one step at a time
checking which operations an action or script just performed
avoid: keeping alternative versions: history is gone when the document closes; duplicate the artboard or save a copy
going back and then editing discards the later states: duplicate the art first if you may want them

cards.name: Image Trace
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Image Trace panel, the settings for live tracing: with a placed or embedded raster image (or a live trace object) selected you pick a preset or mode (colour, grayscale, black and white), palette and colour count or threshold, and under Advanced the paths, corners, noise and method, and the image is converted into flat-colour vector shapes. Does nothing until an image is selected.
cards.how: Select the image, open the panel, choose a preset (High Color, Black & White, Outline ...) or a Mode, tune Colors or Threshold and the Advanced Paths / Corners / Noise sliders, click Trace (or tick Preview), then Object > Image Trace > Expand for editable paths.
use_for: turning a scanned sketch or hand lettering into vector line art
vectorising a low-resolution client logo for print
posterised, flat-colour illustration from a photo
avoid: images that must stay photographic: tracing gives flat colour shapes; keep the raster image
very detailed, many-colour images: thousands of paths and a heavy file; reduce Colors or simplify the image first
cards.script_api: None: no executeMenuCommand id could be paired. The harvest's only route is the menu path / Win32 command 2147484069. Object model: placedItem.trace() or rasterItem.trace() returns a PluginItem; set pluginItem.tracing.tracingOptions (e.g. loadFromPreset("[High Color]"), tracingMode, threshold, maxColors), then pluginItem.tracing.expandTracing() (unverified).

cards.name: Info
cards.id: internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-info
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Info panel, a read-out of the pointer's X / Y position, the selection's width and height (distance and angle while measuring or moving) and the fill and stroke colour values of the selected object. Read-only: nothing in the artwork changes.
use_for: checking an object's exact size and position against a print spec
reading the CMYK / RGB values of a fill when matching brand colours
measuring the distance between two elements with the Measure tool
avoid: changing sizes or positions: use the Transform or Properties panel, Info only displays values
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("internal palettes posing as plug-in menus-info") shows or hides the panel (paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). The same values from a script: pageItem.position, .width, .height and pathItem.fillColor / .strokeColor (unverified).

cards.name: Layers
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Layers panel, the stacking list of the document's layers, sublayers, groups and objects: reorder by dragging, lock, hide, rename, add layers, click the target circle to select an object or apply appearance to a whole layer, and make clipping masks or template layers from its menu.
use_for: organising a complex illustration into named layers (background, art, type)
locking a background while editing the art above it
finding and selecting a buried object
preparing layers for export as separate files or for After Effects
avoid: hundreds of unnamed <Path> items in deep nesting: hard to navigate; name and group as you go
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AdobeLayerPalette1") shows or hides the panel (paired by shortcut, not confirmed by execution). Layers from a script: app.activeDocument.layers.add(), layer.name / .locked / .visible, layer.zOrder(ZOrderMethod.BRINGTOFRONT), pageItem.move(layer, ElementPlacement.PLACEATBEGINNING) (unverified).

cards.name: Libraries
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Creative Cloud Libraries panel: shared libraries of colours, colour themes, character and paragraph styles and graphics, synced through the Adobe account so the same brand assets appear in Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and other apps. Needs Creative Cloud sign-in and sync to be useful.
use_for: keeping a client's logo, brand colours and type styles in one place for every project
dragging a shared graphic into a layout
sharing assets with a team or between Illustrator and Photoshop
avoid: offline or unattended pipelines: the panel depends on sign-in and sync; keep assets as local files or swatch libraries
linked library graphics change when the library changes: embed or unlink if the design must stay fixed

cards.name: Links
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Links panel, the list of every placed file in the document (linked or embedded images, PDFs, other Illustrator files) with icons for missing or modified links. From it you relink, update, go to a link, edit the original, embed or unembed, and read link info such as file name, format, size and resolution.
use_for: swapping low-resolution placeholder images for the final files before print
fixing missing-link warnings after a project folder moves
embedding all images before handing off a single file
checking the effective resolution of placed photos
avoid: collecting a job for the printer: File > Package gathers links and fonts more safely than embedding by hand

cards.name: Magic Wand
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Magic Wand panel, the options of the Magic Wand tool: tick which attributes count as similar (fill colour, stroke colour, stroke weight, opacity, blending mode) and set a tolerance for each except blending mode, which must match; a click with the tool then selects every object whose attributes fall within those tolerances. Double-clicking the tool opens the same panel.
use_for: selecting every shape of roughly the same colour in a traced illustration to recolour or delete it
grabbing all lines of a similar weight in a map or diagram
cleaning up an Image Trace result by selecting the near-white shapes
avoid: exact matches only: Select > Same > Fill Color is simpler and exact
selecting pixels in an image: it works on vector objects, not raster pixels
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("AI Magic Wand") shows or hides the panel (paired by menu words, not confirmed by execution). A script does the same selection by looping over pageItems and comparing fillColor, strokeWidth, opacity and blendingMode (unverified).

cards.name: Mockup

The panel's exact contents in 30.2 (sample images, online requirement) were not recorded.
cards.how: Select the art (and your own photo if you use one), open the panel, choose the mockup image, then adjust the art's position, size and rotation on the surface; re-edit later with Object > Mockup > Edit.
use_for: showing a client a logo on a T-shirt, mug or package
portfolio presentation shots of brand work
quick social posts previewing a print design
avoid: final print or production art: a mockup is a presentation preview; export the flat art separately
strongly folded or reflective surfaces: the fit can look fake; composite in Photoshop with a smart object instead

cards.name: Pathfinder

cutting one shape out of another (Minus Front) for a knockout
dividing overlapping shapes into separate pieces to colour individually

cards.name: Stroke
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Stroke panel: stroke weight, cap and corner (join) style with miter limit, align stroke (center, inside, outside), dashed lines with dash and gap lengths, arrowheads at start and end with scale and alignment, and variable width profiles for the selected paths.

dashed cut and fold lines on packaging dielines
arrows for diagrams and infographics

cards.name: SVG Interactivity

attaching a script reference to an SVG infographic
avoid: modern web work: add events in the site's own code or CSS; the newer Export As SVG route may not keep them

cards.name: Other Library...

use_for: loading a client's brand palette shared as an .ase file
reusing the swatches of an earlier project file
loading a printer's spot-colour set supplied as an .ase file
avoid: a built-in library such as a Pantone book: open it from Window > Swatch Libraries directly
assets kept in sync across apps or a team: use the Libraries panel
